lessons.title: Working tree
lessons.summary: The checked-out files being edited.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Uncommitted changes are distinct from committed history.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: A developer wants to know which local files changed. Inspect git status and the relevant diff.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: It is always identical to the latest commit. This is not a sound assumption; the checked-out files being edited.

lessons.takeaway: Uncommitted changes are distinct from committed history.

lessons.title: Staging
lessons.summary: The proposed contents of the next commit.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Staging selected changes supports focused commits.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: One file contains unrelated fixes that should be separate commits. Stage relevant hunks and review the staged diff.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: Staging automatically pushes changes to the remote. This is not a sound assumption; the proposed contents of the next commit.

lessons.takeaway: Staging selected changes supports focused commits.

lessons.title: Commits
lessons.summary: A snapshot with metadata and parent relationships.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Commit identifiers change when commit contents or metadata change.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: An amended commit has a different hash despite similar files. Recognize that amended metadata creates a new commit object.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: A commit is only a mutable branch name. This is not a sound assumption; a snapshot with metadata and parent relationships.

lessons.takeaway: Commit identifiers change when commit contents or metadata change.

lessons.title: Branches
lessons.summary: A movable reference to a commit.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Creating a branch does not copy an entire independent repository.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: A new local branch is invisible to teammates. Push the intended branch reference when ready to share.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: A branch is a separate physical copy of every historical file. This is not a sound assumption; a movable reference to a commit.

lessons.takeaway: Creating a branch does not copy an entire independent repository.

lessons.title: Fetch
lessons.summary: Download remote objects and update remote-tracking references.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Fetching does not itself merge changes into the current branch.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: A developer wants to inspect remote changes before integration. Fetch and compare the relevant references.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: Fetch automatically discards every local modification. This is not a sound assumption; download remote objects and update remote-tracking references.

lessons.takeaway: Fetching does not itself merge changes into the current branch.

lessons.title: Merge
lessons.summary: A commit joining multiple lines of history.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Merge conflict resolution must preserve intended behavior.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: Two branches merge cleanly but their combined behavior breaks tests. Run integration checks and inspect the interacting changes.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: Every merge rewrites all existing commits. This is not a sound assumption; a commit joining multiple lines of history.

lessons.takeaway: Merge conflict resolution must preserve intended behavior.

lessons.title: Ignore rules
lessons.summary: It does not automatically untrack files already committed.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Sensitive files should be excluded before entering history.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: A credential was committed before an ignore rule was added. Rotate the credential and handle repository exposure deliberately.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: Adding a secret to gitignore removes it from all past commits. This is not a sound assumption; it does not automatically untrack files already committed.

lessons.takeaway: Sensitive files should be excluded before entering history.

lessons.title: Diffs
lessons.summary: The exact changes intended for the next commit.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Generated or unrelated changes deserve deliberate review.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: A commit includes a local debug setting accidentally. Inspect and unstage the unintended change.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: Only filenames matter when reviewing a commit. This is not a sound assumption; the exact changes intended for the next commit.

lessons.takeaway: Generated or unrelated changes deserve deliberate review.

lessons.title: Rebase
lessons.summary: Replay commits onto a different base with new identities.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Rewriting shared history requires coordination.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: A developer rebases commits others have already based work on. Coordinate the rewrite and recovery expectations before publishing.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: Rebase preserves every replayed commit hash unchanged. This is not a sound assumption; replay commits onto a different base with new identities.

lessons.takeaway: Rewriting shared history requires coordination.

lessons.title: Revert
lessons.summary: A new commit that reverses selected changes.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Reverting can preserve published history.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: A bad change is already on a shared production branch. Create and verify a reversal appropriate to the deployed change.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: Revert erases the original commit from every clone. This is not a sound assumption; a new commit that reverses selected changes.

lessons.takeaway: Reverting can preserve published history.

lessons.title: Reset
lessons.summary: It can discard tracked working-tree and index changes.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Inspect and preserve needed work before destructive local operations.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: A developer wants to remove one commit but has valuable uncommitted edits. Preserve the edits and choose the appropriate history operation.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: A hard reset always saves every uncommitted edit. This is not a sound assumption; it can discard tracked working-tree and index changes.

lessons.takeaway: Inspect and preserve needed work before destructive local operations.

lessons.title: Cherry-pick
lessons.summary: Apply selected commit changes onto the current branch.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Dependencies of the selected change may need separate consideration.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: A hotfix is needed without unrelated feature work. Check dependencies and apply only the verified fix.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: Cherry-pick always imports the entire source branch. This is not a sound assumption; apply selected commit changes onto the current branch.

lessons.takeaway: Dependencies of the selected change may need separate consideration.

lessons.title: Conflict resolution
lessons.summary: The intended combined behavior of both changes.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Tests and domain understanding matter beyond removing markers.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: A conflict affects a security check modified on both branches. Understand both changes and test the merged behavior.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: Choosing one side everywhere always preserves intent. This is not a sound assumption; the intended combined behavior of both changes.

lessons.takeaway: Tests and domain understanding matter beyond removing markers.

lessons.title: Reflog
lessons.summary: Recent local reference movements and otherwise hard-to-find commits.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Reflog availability is local and subject to retention.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: A branch pointer was accidentally moved away from recent work. Inspect the local reflog and recover the intended commit reference.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: Reflog is a permanent shared backup of all repository data. This is not a sound assumption; recent local reference movements and otherwise hard-to-find commits.

lessons.takeaway: Reflog availability is local and subject to retention.

lessons.title: Bisect
lessons.summary: A commit associated with a change between known good and bad revisions.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: A reliable reproducible test is essential.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: A regression appeared somewhere in many recent commits. Define a reliable test and narrow the introducing revision.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: Bisect proves a single commit is the complete root cause in every case. This is not a sound assumption; a commit associated with a change between known good and bad revisions.

lessons.takeaway: A reliable reproducible test is essential.

lessons.title: Force with lease
lessons.summary: Reject a rewrite when the remote reference differs from the expected value.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: It still rewrites history and requires deliberate coordination.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: A rewritten branch must be published without overwriting unseen remote work. Check the expected remote state and use a controlled lease.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: It guarantees no collaborator can ever be affected. This is not a sound assumption; reject a rewrite when the remote reference differs from the expected value.

lessons.takeaway: It still rewrites history and requires deliberate coordination.

lessons.title: Continuous integration
lessons.summary: Detect integration problems early through repeatable validation.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Checks should exercise meaningful behavior not just syntax.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: A change passes lint but breaks a user workflow. Add a meaningful behavioral regression check.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: A green build proves the software has no defects. This is not a sound assumption; detect integration problems early through repeatable validation.

lessons.takeaway: Checks should exercise meaningful behavior not just syntax.

lessons.title: Artifacts
lessons.summary: Reduce differences caused by rebuilding during promotion.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Artifact identity and provenance should be recorded.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: Production differs from staging after separate rebuilds. Promote the verified immutable artifact with traceable metadata.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: Rebuilding the same source always produces identical bytes. This is not a sound assumption; reduce differences caused by rebuilding during promotion.

lessons.takeaway: Artifact identity and provenance should be recorded.

lessons.title: CI secrets
lessons.summary: It can execute arbitrary code in the runner context.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Secret access should follow the trust level of the workflow trigger.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: A workflow runs contributor code with deployment credentials. Separate untrusted validation from privileged deployment.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: Any pull request from a public fork is inherently trusted. This is not a sound assumption; it can execute arbitrary code in the runner context.

lessons.takeaway: Secret access should follow the trust level of the workflow trigger.

lessons.title: Dependency pinning
lessons.summary: Reduce surprise changes in third-party execution inputs.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Pinned versions still need a deliberate update process.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: A third-party action changes behavior unexpectedly. Review and pin the intended immutable revision then manage updates.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: Pinning guarantees absence of vulnerabilities forever. This is not a sound assumption; reduce surprise changes in third-party execution inputs.

lessons.takeaway: Pinned versions still need a deliberate update process.

lessons.title: Caching
lessons.summary: Reusing stale or incompatible dependencies or outputs.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Cache keys should reflect relevant inputs and trust boundaries.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: A pipeline passes with cache but fails on a clean runner. Inspect cached assumptions and test clean reproducibility.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: A cache hit proves the build output is correct. This is not a sound assumption; reusing stale or incompatible dependencies or outputs.

lessons.takeaway: Cache keys should reflect relevant inputs and trust boundaries.

lessons.title: Deployment gates
lessons.summary: Required validation and authorization conditions are satisfied.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Gates need clear ownership and useful evidence.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: A deployment is awaiting approval but the test artifact is missing. Require the relevant verified artifact and checks before release.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: A manual click alone proves a release is safe. This is not a sound assumption; required validation and authorization conditions are satisfied.

lessons.takeaway: Gates need clear ownership and useful evidence.

lessons.title: Rollback
lessons.summary: Data or external side effects may be incompatible with the old code.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Rollback plans must include state and schema compatibility.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: A deployment performs an irreversible schema migration. Use a planned compatible migration or verified recovery path.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: Reverting a commit reverses all database writes automatically. This is not a sound assumption; data or external side effects may be incompatible with the old code.

lessons.takeaway: Rollback plans must include state and schema compatibility.

lessons.title: Concurrency controls
lessons.summary: Prevent overlapping changes to the same environment.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Cancellation policy should consider partially applied operations.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: Two releases concurrently modify the same infrastructure. Coordinate deployment ownership and inspect any partial changes.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: Parallel deployment always improves safety. This is not a sound assumption; prevent overlapping changes to the same environment.

lessons.takeaway: Cancellation policy should consider partially applied operations.

lessons.title: OIDC federation
lessons.summary: Obtain short-lived credentials tied to workflow identity.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Trust conditions should constrain repository branch and environment.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: A cloud role trusts any repository in an organization. Narrow the federated identity conditions to intended workloads.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: Federation means every workflow should get administrator access. This is not a sound assumption; obtain short-lived credentials tied to workflow identity.

lessons.takeaway: Trust conditions should constrain repository branch and environment.

lessons.title: Monorepo checks
lessons.summary: Indirect dependencies can be missed by simplistic file filters.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Check selection should model relevant dependency relationships.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: A shared library change skips downstream application tests. Include dependent components in the validation selection.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: A change outside one directory can never affect that component. This is not a sound assumption; indirect dependencies can be missed by simplistic file filters.

lessons.takeaway: Check selection should model relevant dependency relationships.

lessons.title: Release tags
lessons.summary: Trace a release to an intended source or artifact identity.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Tag protection and verification help preserve release meaning.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: A release tag is moved after artifacts were published. Investigate the identity mismatch and preserve an auditable release trail.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: Every tag is intrinsically immutable and unforgeable. This is not a sound assumption; trace a release to an intended source or artifact identity.

lessons.takeaway: Tag protection and verification help preserve release meaning.

lessons.title: Flaky tests
lessons.summary: They weaken confidence that failures indicate real regressions.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Track and fix nondeterminism rather than normalizing blind retries.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: A team reruns failed tests repeatedly without investigation. Record failure patterns and isolate the nondeterministic cause.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: Retrying until green proves correctness. This is not a sound assumption; they weaken confidence that failures indicate real regressions.

lessons.takeaway: Track and fix nondeterminism rather than normalizing blind retries.

lessons.title: Branch protection
lessons.summary: Defined review and status-check requirements before integration.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Rules should match the actual delivery risk and trusted actors.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: A required test is accidentally made optional on the release branch. Restore the intended gate and verify the effective rule behavior.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: Branch protection proves all merged code is bug-free. This is not a sound assumption; defined review and status-check requirements before integration.

lessons.takeaway: Rules should match the actual delivery risk and trusted actors.

lessons.title: Supply-chain evidence
lessons.summary: Which inputs and process produced the artifact.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Provenance is evidence to verify against a trust policy.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: A binary's source revision and build workflow cannot be established. Require traceable build evidence and verify artifact identity.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: Provenance replaces all vulnerability assessment. This is not a sound assumption; which inputs and process produced the artifact.

lessons.takeaway: Provenance is evidence to verify against a trust policy.
